title: Soil heterotrophic respiration assessment using minimally disturbed soil microcosm cores
author: Comeau, Lai, et al.
materials: To test the effectiveness of the minimally disturbed soil microcosm cores to assess soil heterotrophic respiration, we performed incubations on a set of samples with different temperature and soil moisture levels. Briefly, four control plots were selected at the Tai Po Kau Nature Reserve Research Station in Hong Kong [17]. Four 98 cm3 (inner diameter 5 cm, height 5 cm) intact soil cores were extracted in each plot. The procedures described above were followed. The incubations were conducted in a factorial design with 4 WHC (30, 48, 66 and 84%) and 4 temperatures (14 °C, 20 °C, 26 °C and 32 °C). The CO2 concentrations were analyzed with a gas chromatograph (GC system 7890 A, Agilent Technologies) equipped with a flame ionization detector and an electron capture detector to quantify CO2. The calculated carbon effluxes were plotted with a Gaussian 3D regression fitted curve following Eq. (8) using SigmaPlot version 10.0 (Systat Software, San Jose, CA).(8)fx,y=a.×exp-0.5.×x-xob2+y-yoc2.a, b and c are constant coefficients; x is the soil temperature (°C); y is the soil moisture (%); x0 is the average temperature; y0 is the average soil moisture.

steps.title: Collect undisturbed field soil cores
steps.instruction: Using bulk‑density rings, extract intact soil cores of 98 cm³ (inner diameter 5 cm, height 5 cm) vertically from the 0–5 cm depth. Collect 4–10 cores per treatment (or per field plot) and place them immediately in coolers with ice packs.

steps.title: Weigh cores and obtain bulk density subsample
steps.instruction: In the laboratory, weigh each core, carefully retrieve the soil, and take a 20 g subsample from each core. Oven‑dry the subsample at 105 °C to determine bulk density and gravimetric moisture content.

steps.title: Pool cores and remove roots
steps.instruction: Combine the cores per treatment, then remove root systems with great care so as not to destroy small aggregates. Root removal is essential for agricultural or forest soils to avoid abnormal CO₂ pulses from fresh root decomposition.

steps.title: Calculate fresh soil mass for microcosms
steps.instruction: Compute the mass of fresh soil needed to fill a 51 cm³ microcosm using Equation (1): Sn = Vo · Db · (Gv/100 + 1), where Sn is fresh soil (g), Vo is microcosm volume (cm³), Db is bulk density (g cm⁻³), and Gv is gravimetric moisture (%).

steps.title: Repack soil into microcosm cores
steps.instruction: Repack the calculated amount of soil into each 51 cm³ microcosm tube at the field bulk density, creating two layers: fill the bottom half (2.5 cm thick) first, then add the remaining soil to the top half (2.5 cm thick) to improve bulk‑density uniformity.

steps.title: Adjust soil moisture to target level
steps.instruction: Adjust the moisture of each microcosm to the desired gravimetric water content by adding drops of deionized water or by air‑drying for several hours. The water volume required is calculated with Equation (2): Wa = Wm + Wf + (Vo·Db·(Dw/100 + 1)) – Wm + Wf + (Vo·Db·(Cw/100 + 1)), where Wa is water needed (ml), Wm is empty tube weight (g), Wf is moist filter weight (g), Dw is desired moisture (%), and Cw is current moisture (%).

steps.title: Seal microcosms with Parafilm
steps.instruction: Cover each microcosm tube with Parafilm® to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Pre‑incubate microcosms in sealed containers
steps.instruction: Place the sealed microcosms in a hermetically sealed plastic container (minimum volume 2.5 L, height ≥ 15 cm) and incubate at 25 °C for two weeks to allow soil stabilization. Ensure the container is large enough so the sampling needle will not strike a microcosm.

steps.title: Discard germinated microcosms and re‑weigh
steps.instruction: After the two‑week pre‑incubation, discard any microcosms containing germinated seeds. Weigh the remaining microcosms again to verify that soil moisture has not changed during pre‑incubation.

steps.title: Incubate and sample headspace gases
steps.instruction: Incubate the microcosms at 25 °C (or other desired temperatures). At 0, 48, and 96 h after sealing the incubation container, withdraw a 20 ml gas sample with an airtight syringe through a septum. Immediately before sampling, homogenize the headspace by pumping air in and out with a 60 ml syringe for 15 s (or use an internal micro‑fan). Analyze CO₂ concentration within 48 h using a gas chromatograph (GC) or an infrared gas analyzer (IRGA).

steps.title: Construct microcosm tubes
steps.instruction: Use transparent polystyrene vials (60 ml, 36 mm inside diameter). Drill four evenly spaced 0.8 mm holes in the bottom of each vial. Label each tube and record its weight. Cut laboratory filter paper (pore size 20–25 µm) into disks that fit the tube bottom, add three drops of deionized water to each disk, gently shake off excess water, weigh the wet disks, and place them at the bottom of the tube. Draw reference lines on the outside at 2.5 cm and 5 cm from the base to guide the two‑layer repacking.

steps.title: Determine soil water holding capacity
steps.instruction: Compact fresh soil to its field bulk density in a 51 ml microcosm as described for incubation. Saturate the microcosm by ponding water, cover the top with Parafilm®, and place the tube on a 2 mm sieve to drain excess water in the dark at 25 °C for 10 h without external pressure. Weigh the saturated microcosm and calculate water holding capacity (WHC) using Equation (6): WHC = (WSM – Wm – Wf – (Vo·Db)) / (Vo·Db), where WSM is the weight of the water‑saturated microcosm (g).

steps.title: Compute 50% WHC gravimetric water content
steps.instruction: For standard incubations, set soil moisture to 50 % WHC. Calculate the corresponding gravimetric water content using Equation (7): Dw50 = (WSM – Wm – Wf – Vo·Db·0.50) / (Vo·100), where Dw50 is the gravimetric water content at 50 % WHC (%).
